prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1296; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle struck the rear of claimant's vehicle at low speed. Police report requested. Insured states he was stopped and was struck from behind before contact, so liability is under review. Photos of both vehicles received from insured and await review.

Entry 2: Claimant's attorney's office contacted this adjuster and confirmed representation. All further communication to go through counsel. Claimant reports a wrist fracture sustained in the collision and is currently in a cast. Requested medical authorization forms and itemized treatment records. Advised counsel that a recorded statement from the claimant is not required at this time.

Entry 3: Received police report. Report notes the insured vehicle was the striking vehicle and that the insured made no admission at the scene. Witness statement from a bystander reviewed and consistent with the report. Liability assessment updated to probable fault on insured, pending final review by supervisor.

Entry 4: Counsel submitted medical records covering emergency room visit and orthopedic follow-up. Records document a fracture to the wrist with surgical consultation recommended. Reviewed records with the medical review unit. Requested clarification from treating physician on expected recovery timeline and any need for further procedures. Reserve adjusted to reflect injury severity.

Entry 5: Counsel sent a written demand package including medical bills, wage loss documentation, and a request for settlement. Demand under review. Scheduled internal conference with supervisor to discuss valuation and negotiation strategy. Notified insured that the claim is active and that no admission of fault has been made to the claimant. Diary set for follow-up with counsel in two weeks.
